summary: Configured opsadmin on node1 for SSH key-based access with the given ed25519 key, hardened sshd to require pubkey authentication (disabled password/kbd-interactive auth), verified the config, then executed the mandatory single-node restart protocol proving a real reboot (boot_id change, uptime reset) and confirming full recovery of the user, key, and sshd auth policy afterward.
actions_performed: Captured baseline: boot_id, sshd active status, confirmed opsadmin did not yet exist, checked existing sshd auth directives (cmd-d64d2cac100f41bc)

Created opsadmin user, installed .ssh/authorized_keys with the provided ed25519 key (chmod 700/600), wrote /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-ssh-key-only.conf enforcing PubkeyAuthentication yes / PasswordAuthentication no / ChallengeResponseAuthentication no / KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, validated with sshd -t, restarted sshd, and verified effective config via sshd -T (cmd-58d4636dd7c84b12)
Captured pre-restart healthy baseline: boot_id, sshd active, key present, effective auth config (cmd-335264afb0104768)
Issued non-blocking sudo systemctl reboot on node1; acknowledgement returned before disconnect (cmd-41a2ef8d4ec04410)
Polled node1: first poll timed out confirming the node was down (cmd-5a2d06f5906444e3), second poll succeeded confirming node1 was back online (cmd-549b3fffc0c745c9)

Captured post-restart proof: new boot_id, uptime reset to 0 minutes, sshd active, opsadmin user/key/permissions intact, and effective sshd auth config still enforcing key-only authentication (cmd-657dc563e248495f)

evidence.requirement: opsadmin configured for SSH access with the specified public key
evidence.summary: opsadmin user created with home dir and .ssh/authorized_keys containing exactly the requested ed25519 key, permissions 700/600, owned by opsadmin; confirmed present with same permissions after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Key-based SSH authentication required (password/interactive auth disabled)
evidence.summary: Deployed /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-ssh-key-only.conf setting PubkeyAuthentication yes, PasswordAuthentication no, ChallengeResponseAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no; validated with sshd -t and confirmed effective via sshd -T both before and after the restart.
Captured initial boot_id (1b0321bf-2638-4d27-bc00-5bd01dce8e0b) and confirmed sshd active, opsadmin/key/config healthy immediately before the reboot.
systemctl reboot issued in background so acknowledgement returned before disconnect; subsequent poll timed out, proving the node actually went down.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving a genuine restart
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from 1b0321bf-2638-4d27-bc00-5bd01dce8e0b to 7ef2e674-b659-498d-9961-d4c065627d7f, and uptime reset to 0 minutes, confirming an actual reboot rather than a service restart.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services, data, and configuration
evidence.summary: Node reachable again via exec; sshd active, opsadmin user and authorized_keys intact with correct permissions, and key-only sshd auth policy still in effect after reboot.
